transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you all know, we've got a 48-hour water conservation restriction from the municipal water authority, and I need to put together a water-control plan before we proceed. We've got 2,400 liters of reclaimed water available, and both Line X and Line Y are scheduled to run during the restriction. Before I make my final decision on how to allocate our process water, I'd like to hear the updates from quality, maintenance, and EHS. Who'd like to start?

Line X's process limit is 1,200, so the reclaimed water exceeds that limit and is not acceptable for Line X. Line Y's process limit is 2,200, so the reclaimed water is within spec for Line Y. transcript.text: I need to share an important maintenance update. My inspection of the recovery skid, documented in my maintenance notebook but not yet entered in the work-order system, found that the skid requires an exact 3-hour membrane flush before use and can then deliver reclaimed water at no more than 600 liters per hour. This means if we plan to use the reclaimed water, we need to account for that 3-hour flush time and the 600 liters-per-hour delivery rate in our scheduling.

transcript.text: I need to share an important EHS update from my permit review with the municipal inspector yesterday. That review, which is awaiting attachment to the site's permit record, found two critical requirements: reclaimed water may be used only after its residual sanitizer is adjusted to exactly 0.3 parts per million, and each use day requires a signed sanitizer log. So in addition to the conductivity and maintenance considerations, we'll need to verify the sanitizer level is adjusted to exactly 0.3 ppm and have a signed sanitizer log for each day we use reclaimed water.

decisions.reclaimed_water_plan: Allocate 1,800 liters of reclaimed water to Line Y only, as the reclaimed water conductivity of 1,800 µS/cm exceeds Line X's 1,200 µS/cm limit but is within Line Y's 2,200 µS/cm limit. Line X will not receive reclaimed water during the restriction period. The remaining 600 liters of reclaimed water will be held in reserve. Before use, the recovery skid must undergo a 3-hour membrane flush, after which reclaimed water can be delivered at 600 liters per hour. The residual sanitizer must be adjusted to exactly 0.3 ppm, and a signed sanitizer log is required for each day of use. The conductivity test completed by Ravi must be recorded in the quality folder before reclaimed water is used on Line Y.

commitments.detail: Ravi must upload the reclaimed-water conductivity test result (1,800 µS/cm) to the shared quality folder before Line Y begins using reclaimed water.
Mei must enter the recovery skid inspection findings in the work-order system and schedule the 3-hour membrane flush before reclaimed water delivery begins.

Jon must ensure the residual sanitizer is adjusted to exactly 0.3 ppm and that a signed sanitizer log is prepared for each day of reclaimed water use. The permit review findings must be attached to the site's permit record.
Elena will determine an alternative process-water source for Line X during the restriction period, since reclaimed water is not acceptable for Line X due to conductivity limits.
